tools_used: WebFetch (supremecourt.gov docket JSON and reply PDF)
pypdf (local text extraction of the fetched reply)
helpful: Provisioned petition, BIO, and QP text with documents.json — the core of the forecast
sal-v4 band table with bracketed reached rates per Term — a clean, leakage-safe anchor
supremecourt.gov docket JSON for the companion petition's status
gaps: No statpack cut for 'response requested after waiver' — the strongest signal on this docket has no published conditional rate
The reply brief is not provisioned even though it is on the docket before the redistribution; a cert cell routinely wants it
fedcourts query has no caption/topic filter for SCOTUS rows, so it cannot retrieve doctrinally similar petitions; its --citation filter is served off ~200 rows
CourtListener holds no docket entries for SCOTUS paid petitions here (0 for 25-958), so companion-petition status had to come from supremecourt.gov
Amicus briefs are listed on the docket but not provisioned; an amicus count feature is deferred in salience
notes: The 'distributed twice' state here is a CFR redistribution, not a post-conference relist; a CFR flag in context.json would let predictors condition on it directly.
